'''''The Invite''''' is a 2026 American [[comedy drama]] film directed by [[Olivia Wilde]] from a screenplay by [[Will McCormack]] and [[Rashida Jones]]. It is an English-language remake of the 2020 Spanish film ''[[The People Upstairs (2020 film)|The People Upstairs]]'' (''Sentimental'') by [[Cesc Gay]]. The film stars [[Seth Rogen]], Wilde, [[Penélope Cruz]], and [[Edward Norton]].

The film premiered at the [[Eccles Theater]] as a part of the [[2026 Sundance Film Festival]] on January 24, receiving generally positive reviews. It received a [[limited theatrical release|limited release]] in the United States on June 26, before opening wide on July 10, by [[A24]], and has grossed $38.9 million worldwide.

==Plot==
In [[San Francisco]], failed [[musician]] Joe arrives home from his job as a [[jazz band]] teacher at a [[Music school|conservatory]] to discover his stay-at-home wife Angela has invited their upstairs neighbors, divorcée Piña and widower Hawk, over for dinner at their apartment. Joe and Angela's marriage is rocky and they bicker constantly, most recently over the loud sex sounds they often hear from upstairs. Joe plans to confront the couple, but Angela, who is desperate to impress the neighbors, demands he keep calm and quiet.

Piña and Hawk arrive at the apartment as Joe and Angela are mid-argument. Unprepared to host a dinner party, Angela makes several awkward mistakes, such as not having any wine and not checking Piña's dietary restrictions. Meanwhile, Joe openly antagonizes the couple, but is surprised to see they are impressed by his brutally honest nature. The group eventually warm up to one another, although Joe still resents his neighbors for their noise and is troubled when he learns Hawk has seen Angela naked through a window.

Later that night, Piña and Hawk apologize for the noise they make during sex and reveal to Joe and Angela that they participate in [[Orgy|sex parties]] which is the reason for the noise; Joe and Angela are titillated by this discovery. Piña admits that she and Hawk came to the dinner party hoping to invite Joe and Angela to have [[group sex]] with them. Joe and Angela are eager, but Piña, who is a [[Sexology|sexologist]], is unsure after seeing the couple fight throughout the night. Instead, they decide to [[Swinging (sexual practice)|swap partners]]. However, Angela is too nervous to initiate sex with Hawk while Joe falls while dancing with Piña and hurts his back.

Another argument erupts between Joe and Angela, and he berates their neighbors. Piña gets the couple to talk about their relationship, and learns of the resentment they have to each other and the fact they have not had sex in a year. Piña suggests the couple should separate instead of sticking together for the sake of their daughter, Maggie, or find a way to reframe their relationship, as the current status appears to have run its course. Angela and Joe seemingly agree to separate, and discuss their next moves, but upon returning from the kitchen, discover Piña and Hawk have left. Joe returns to his office and plays his piano, which he had previously refused to play out of shame at his failed career, with Angela eventually joining him.

==Reception==
===Box office===
{{As of|2026|8|5|df=US}}, ''The Invite'' has grossed $22.8 million in the United States and Canada, and $16.1 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $38.9 million.<ref name="BOM"/><ref name="NUM"/>

The film made $379,000 in Los Angeles and $54,000 in New York City from [[Limited theatrical release|limited release]] screenings in its first weekend, all of which were sold out,<ref name="BoxOfficeLimited">{{cite web |title=Rare Summer Comedy 'The Invite' Banks a Top Limited Opening of the Year – Specialty Box Office |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=June 28, 2026 |access-date=July 1, 2026 |url=https://deadline.com/2026/06/indie-film-box-offiice-comedy-the-invite-top-limited-opening-1236969226/ |archive-date=July 1, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260701104057/https://deadline.com/2026/06/indie-film-box-offiice-comedy-the-invite-top-limited-opening-1236969226/ |url-status=live}}</ref> becoming one of the top per-screen openings of the year.<ref name="NationalExpansion">{{cite web |title='The Invite' Dines Out at No. 6 for Weekend in Solid National Expansion; 'Reading Lolita in Tehran' at the Angelika – Specialty Box Office |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=July 12, 2026 |access-date=July 12, 2026 |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/indie-film-box-office-the-invite-no-6-1236980119/}}</ref>

During its first weekend in the United Kingdom, it grossed £799,382 (approximately $1.06 million) and came in third place.<ref name="UK">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/toy-story-5-minions-monsters-uk-ireland-box-office-1236803117/ |title='Toy Story 5' Holds No. 1 as 'Minions & Monsters' Chases at U.K. and Ireland Box Office |last=Ramachandran |first=Naman |author-link=Naman Ramachandran |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 7, 2026 |access-date=July 7, 2026 |archive-date=July 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260707101445/https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/toy-story-5-minions-monsters-uk-ireland-box-office-1236803117/ |url-status=live}}</ref> The United States wide expansion opened to 1,610 locations (up from 28 screens) in its third weekend, grossing over $5.7 million for a $7.38 million cume and coming in sixth place at the domestic box office.<ref name="NationalExpansion"/>

extract:
The Invite is a 2026 American comedy drama film directed by Olivia Wilde from a screenplay by Will McCormack and Rashida Jones. It is an English-language remake of the 2020 Spanish film The People Upstairs (Sentimental) by Cesc Gay. The film stars Seth Rogen, Wilde, Penélope Cruz, and Edward Norton.
The film premiered at the Eccles Theater as a part of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival on January 24, receiving generally positive reviews. It received a limited release in the United States on June 26, before opening wide on July 10, by A24, and has grossed $38.9 million worldwide.
